title: Clubs and stationary sets: unavoidable subsets of uncountable ordinals

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 61–64 (§14, through Theorem 14.14; uncountability and nonempty closure conditions made explicit)

summary: Closed unbounded sets provide a notion of largeness on regular uncountable ordinals.
abstract: An unbounded set of ordinals can still miss all limit ordinals: the successor ordinals are an example. Clubs, or closed unbounded sets, reach arbitrarily high ordinals and also contain the limit points they approach within the ambient ordinal. At the first uncountable ordinal, countably many clubs still have a club as their intersection. A stationary set meets every club, giving a stronger kind of largeness than unboundedness.
